title: Dropping his instruments while travelling through Chicago
summary: Howard tells of his cornet, clarinet and saxophone falling off a ride on his way to California via Chicago.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Okay, so we'll just leave him here. There was one story you told too, if you remember, something about, it seems like to me on the other tape, when you were coming to California and something about your instruments falling off of a wagon.
Oh, yeah.
Can you say what that story was?
Sure.
I still don't remember it. What happened to them?
They fell off of the -- you know how they put your things in kind of a -- oh, I don't know.
Wagon?
No, it wasn't a wagon.
You were getting a ride with somebody?
Yeah, I was getting a ride from one station to the next station.
Was this someone who worked for the railroad? Who was driving this cart or whatever it was?
They didn't work for the railroad.
They just worked for themselves.
And you caught a ride. Was it a taxi -- was it like somebody that you had to pay for the ride?
No, I didn't have to pay them.
Why did they pick you up then?
Well, they knew me and knew what I was trying to do, trying to go somewhere.
Then what happened, your instruments fell?
Well, my instruments fell, yeah.
Did it damage them?
No, didn't hurt them at all. The only thing that hurt me, because I knew I was going to get in trouble, with hurting my instruments.
So at that time did you have quite a few instruments with you, saxophone and everything?
Had a saxophone and a trumpet.
Clarinet and trumpet.
Clarinet, saxophone and cornet.
Yeah, cornet, that's what it was, I knew it --
Now, was that in Chicago?
Chicago, yeah, coming down --
So you were on the way to Chicago.
On his way, because I remember -- he was on his way to California and went through Chicago and that
was when it happened.
Yeah, that's when it happened.
So you made your train all right.
Oh, yeah.
